cycleModes.name: Light Soil Cycle (2 Hours, 800°F / 427°C)
cycleModes.description: Shortest pyrolytic cycle intended for light dust and minimal cooking splatter. Operates well above the 500°F (260°C) thermal degradation point of fluoropolymers and readily pyrolyzes surface oils into airborne smoke and carbonaceous particulates.

cycleModes.name: Standard Self-Clean Cycle (3 Hours, 875°F / 468°C)
cycleModes.description: The standard factory self-clean setting programmed into residential ovens. Sustained cavity temperatures exceed 875°F (468°C), causing severe thermal decomposition of all organic residue, extensive fluoropolymer breakdown, and active carbon monoxide generation.

cycleModes.name: Heavy / Encrusted Soil Cycle (4.5 Hours, 932°F / 500°C)
cycleModes.description: Maximum thermal intensity cycle designed for heavily blackened, baked-on grease. Sustained 500°C (932°F) heats cause violent pyrolysis of grease, generating massive plumes of carbon monoxide, toxic VOCs, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and ultrafine particulate matter.

cycleModes.name: Low-Temp Steam Clean / AquaClean (40 Mins, 250°F / 121°C)
cycleModes.description: Non-pyrolytic hydrothermal cycle utilizing distilled water in the bottom reservoir. Heats to only 250°F (121°C), producing zero fluoropolymer off-gassing, zero carbon monoxide, zero toxic fumes, and zero risk to pet birds or humans.

soilLoads.name: Trace / Pristine (Light Cooking Dust < 5g)
soilLoads.description: Minimal cooking residue, light dust, and transparent micro-splatters. Still generates detectable acrolein and particulate matter as heated air expands past door gaskets.

soilLoads.name: Moderate Soil (Spotted Walls & Base, ~25g Grease)
soilLoads.description: Typical residential oven with baked-on oil rings from roasting chickens, pizza drips, and roasted vegetables. Pyrolysis releases pungent acrolein smoke, irritating throat and eyes.

soilLoads.name: Heavy Encrusted (Blackened Grease & Sugar Pools, ~80g)
soilLoads.description: Thick blackened pools of baked-on fat, meat drippings, and pie fruit sugar. Pyrolysis generates dense yellowish-gray smoke plumes, sharp acrolein, formaldehyde, and potentially dangerous carbon monoxide spikes.

soilLoads.name: Catastrophic Spill: Forgotten Teflon Oven Liner (~60g Pure PTFE)
soilLoads.description: A non-stick fluoropolymer oven floor mat accidentally left inside before activating the self-clean cycle. At 450°C–500°C, the entire 60g sheet pyrolyzes directly into toxic fluorocarbon gases (carbonyl fluoride COF2, perfluoroisobutylene PFIB, trifluoroacetic acid TFA), creating lethal concentrations for pet birds and severe acute chemical pneumonitis in humans.

fluoropolymerSources.name: OEM Vitreous Enamel + Braided Fiberglass Gasket (Zero PTFE)
fluoropolymerSources.description: Traditional oven construction with porcelain-coated carbon steel cavity, nickel-plated steel racks, and braided silica/fiberglass door gasket. Free of fluoropolymers, releasing only combustion particulates from burning food grease.

fluoropolymerSources.name: Flexible Silicone Gasket with PTFE Anti-Adhesion Coating
fluoropolymerSources.description: Modern perimeter door gasket featuring silicone rubber treated with a low-friction fluoropolymer surface coating to prevent door sticking under intense heat. Thermally begins shedding sub-100nm ultrafine particles at 260°C (500°F).

fluoropolymerSources.name: True Convection Fan Motor with PTFE Wiring Insulation & Baffle
fluoropolymerSources.description: True European convection ovens incorporate a rear motorized fan blade and high-temperature electrical leads insulated with fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) or PTFE. Air currents actively circulate hot pyrolytic fumes across these components.

fluoropolymerSources.name: Aftermarket 'Non-Stick' Easy-Clean Racks or Catalytic Side Panels
fluoropolymerSources.category: Coated Cookware / Accessories Left in Oven
fluoropolymerSources.description: Racks or catalytic panels coated with dark non-stick PTFE finish mistakenly left inside during self-cleaning. Factory manuals strictly instruct users to remove all racks before self-cleaning to avoid destroying the finish and releasing toxic fumes.

fluoropolymerSources.name: Accidental Forgotten Non-Stick Oven Mat / Liner on Cavity Floor
fluoropolymerSources.description: Severe hazard scenario where a flexible PTFE/fiberglass oven protector liner is left on the bottom floor. Direct radiant contact with the 900°F (482°C) lower heating element causes catastrophic thermal pyrolysis within minutes.

ventilationEnvironments.name: Closed Windows, No Active Hood (0.35 Air Changes/Hr)
ventilationEnvironments.description: Winter or summer climate with sealed double-pane windows, closed interior doors, and either no range hood or an unpowered microwave hood. Fumes accumulate continuously throughout the living space over 4 hours.

ventilationEnvironments.name: Microwave Recirculating Charcoal Filter Hood (0.8 ACH)
ventilationEnvironments.description: Recirculating vent hood that blows air through a coarse mesh grease screen and thin charcoal pad back into the kitchen at eye level. Does NOT remove carbon monoxide, ultrafine particles, or fluoropolymer fumes.

ventilationEnvironments.name: Exterior Ducted Range Hood on High (300 CFM, ~3.0 ACH)
ventilationEnvironments.description: Dedicated overhead range hood exhausted directly outdoors through a 6-inch rigid duct. Captures roughly 60% to 75% of oven vent plumes, significantly depressing indoor pollutant peaks.

ventilationEnvironments.name: Commercial-Grade Hood (600+ CFM) + Open Cross-Breeze Windows (6.5 ACH)
ventilationEnvironments.description: Maximum dilution environment with wide-open opposing windows, ceiling fan on high, and high-CFM exterior ducting. Rapidly dilutes fumes, reducing indoor steady-state concentrations by up to 85%.

vulnerabilityProfiles.name: Healthy Adult (Baseline Respiratory Resistance)
vulnerabilityProfiles.fumeFeverSusceptibility: Low to Moderate (Transient chills/fever if fumes heavy)
vulnerabilityProfiles.description: Healthy adult immune and respiratory tract. Exposure to high pyrolysis fumes triggers mucous membrane irritation, coughing, eye watering, and headache, with potential Teflon flu if ventilation is poor.

vulnerabilityProfiles.name: Asthma, COPD, or Bronchial Hyperresponsiveness
vulnerabilityProfiles.description: Airway reactivity provoked by ultrafine particulates (<100nm) and acidic acrolein/COF2 vapors. Can induce immediate acute asthma attacks, persistent coughing spasms, and oxygen desaturation.

vulnerabilityProfiles.name: Infant / Toddler (2x Respiration Rate per kg)
vulnerabilityProfiles.description: Young children inhale significantly more air per kilogram of body weight than adults and spend more time close to floor breathing zones. Highly vulnerable to carbon monoxide and fine particulates.

vulnerabilityProfiles.name: Pet Bird Present (Parrot, Cockatiel, Parakeet, Finch, African Grey)
vulnerabilityProfiles.fumeFeverSusceptibility: EXTREME / LETHAL (Avian Teflon Toxicosis within 15–30 mins)
vulnerabilityProfiles.description: Avian respiratory anatomy features rigid lungs with unidirectional air sacs, an exceptionally thin blood-gas barrier, and high metabolic demand. Inhaled PTFE pyrolysis gases and ultrafine particles cause acute pulmonary hemorrhage, suffocation, and sudden death. Pet birds must ALWAYS be removed completely from the residence.

vulnerabilityProfiles.name: Domestic Dogs / Cats (Indoor Pets)
vulnerabilityProfiles.description: Lacks the hyper-vulnerable air sac physiology of birds, but pets staying on the kitchen floor face concentrated heavier-than-air VOCs and particulates, causing respiratory distress and lethargy.

nonToxicAlternatives.title: Baking Soda & Vinegar Active Saponification Protocol
steps: Mix 1/2 cup of pure baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) with 3 tablespoons of warm water into a spreadable thick paste.
Remove all oven racks, thermometer probes, and pans. Coat all interior enamel walls and floor (avoiding heating elements and electrical igniters).
Allow paste to dwell overnight (10–12 hours) to hydrolyze and saponify baked-on vegetable oils and animal triglycerides.
Wipe away loosened paste with a damp microfiber cloth. Spray remaining residue with distilled white vinegar; the mild foaming carbonic acid reaction lifts stubborn carbonized spots without fumes.

nonToxicAlternatives.title: Hydrothermal Lemon Steam Basin Protocol
steps: Fill a large high-temperature borosilicate glass 9x13 baking dish halfway with warm water.
Cut 2 fresh lemons in half, squeeze the juice into the water, and place the rinds cut-side down into the dish.
Preheat oven to 250°F (121°C) and place the dish on the center rack for 45 to 60 minutes.
Turn off the oven and allow cavity to cool until warm to the touch. The steam and natural d-limonene terpene vapors soften light grease, allowing it to wipe clean effortlessly.
